messages:
maya: quick q — doing a triage on a slow customer call. where's the single source for TTFT p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec breakdown (by model/route/region)? i remember a few dashboards but want the canonical links so i don't send folks to stale panels
chris: use the "Latency & Tokenflow" dashboard in Grafana -> Observability / Platform. panels to check: 'TTFT p50/p95/p99 (route)', 'Tokens/sec by model', and 'Request path token distribution'. link: https://grafana.internal.redwood.io/d/obs/latency-tokenflow (bookmark it)
zane: for traces, jaeger has the end-to-end spans. search by trace id or by tag: http.status, model, route. quick trick: filter for span "serve.request" and sort by duration to find slow TTFT segments
chris: if you want prometheus queries quickly — sample PromQL for tokens/sec (5m):
```
sum by (model) (rate(redwood_tokens_emitted_total[5m]))
```
TTFT p95 by route (10m):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_ttft_bucket[10m])) by (le, route))
```
(might need to adjust buckets depending on release)
maya: perfect — thanks. any recommended thresholds for alerts? we're seeing sporadic p95 spikes ~700ms during afternoon that don't affect p99 much
ryan-oncall: for hosted-prod we currently alert p95 > 500ms sustained for 5m (SEV-3). if p99 > 2s -> SEV-2. for tokens/sec drops (indicating throttling) alert when tokens/sec drops 50% below baseline for 3m. these are in the alert rules repo: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/alerts (see obs/latency.rules)
zane: also consider checking the autoscale and queue depth panels — sometimes high TTFT is due to CPU saturation or batching delays. panels: "GPU utilization" and "request queue depth" on the same dashboard
maya: where's the runbook for a TTFT p95 alert? want to follow steps instead of opening a bunch of tickets
chris: runbook is in Confluence -> Observability -> TTFT Runbook. quick steps: 1) check route-level p95 -> 2) check tokens/sec for the same route -> 3) open Jaeger trace of slow sample -> 4) check backend GPU util / mem -> 5) if it's an infra issue, escalate to eng-runtime oncall
maya: can you paste the runbook link here?
chris: https://confluence.internal.redwood.io/display/OBS/TTFT+Runbook
obs-bot: reminder: there is currently a canary rollout for quantized-1.3 in us-west which can cause transient latency changes. see release note: https://releases.redwood.io/quantized-1.3
maya: ah that explains the afternoon spikes maybe. will correlate timestamps. thanks! :thumbsup:
ryan-oncall: if you find a recurring spike tied to that canary, set a temporary silence on the p95 alert for the canary tag and ping infra to pause the rollout until we investigate
zane: for quick debugging you can also use this jaeger query to find slow ops in the last hour (paste into jaeger search): service=redwood-serve operation="serve.request" duration>500ms tags.model=~".*"
chris: adding a tiny alert tuning note — avoid firing on short-lived noise: use for p95: for 5m window and require >3 distinct hosts contributing to the spike to reduce false positives. that's encoded in obs/latency.rules already
maya: got it. i'll open a short postmortem draft if it persists and link all graphs/traces. thanks everyone :)
chris: np, ping me if you need a graph panel added or want a dedicated dashboard for that customer's route
maya: will do — closing thread. :white_check_mark:
